resources.string: How the knee bends and straightens
A simplified side view of normal knee movement. The thigh is held still for illustration. Angles, forces, distances and timing are not measurements.
Two muscle groups act across the knee
The quadriceps sit in front of the thigh and the hamstrings sit behind. Their tendons link the muscles to bones across the knee.
The hamstrings help bend the knee
When the hamstrings pull from behind, the lower leg can bend back relative to the thigh.
The patella glides as the knee bends
As the lower leg bends, the patella moves along the groove at the front of the femur. It stays connected to the knee extensor tendons.
The quadriceps help straighten the knee
The quadriceps pull through the patella and its tendon onto the tibia, helping the lower leg straighten.
The knee returns toward its starting position
This example separates the main pulls for clarity. In everyday movements the two muscle groups can also be active together.
